title.narrative: Strengthening capacities for sustainability and fundraising of CAFOD partners in Central America

description.narrative: The current situation reported by civil society organisations in Central America is characterised by several issues that affect their capacities for sustainability and fundraising: -There is a decline in the sub-region in terms of resources dedicated by institutional donors, UN agencies, accompanying organisations (similar to CAFOD) and T&F. This is due to several factors, including wars and humanitarian crises. -This has resulted in increased competition for the same resources among civil society organisations. Local organisations must compete among themselves and with other actors (UN, INGOs, etc.) to access the scarce resources available to ensure their survival. - Despite a theoretical discourse that prioritises "localisation", many of these resources are also co-opted by international entities that continue to be more competitive due to their size and capacities. - This also affects the ability of these organisations to effectively lobby and influence donor priorities based on the real needs they encounter in their local and national contexts. The funding available and their priorities remain subjugated to current diplomatic and commercial interests. Led by COMAL, this project aims to support three key areas: R1 - Strengthen knowledge (identification, communication and understanding) of funding opportunities R2 - Improve strategic positioning for funding through technical support (marketing, positioning) and peer-to-peer and consortium approaches R3 - Strengthen capacities for decision-making, design/learning and M&E of proposal development processes.
